title: The Frohmanian Tether on SDiff(T^3): A Metriplectic Correction, Its Canonicity, and an Obstruction to Damping
notes: Copyright (c) 2026 Benjamin Stanley Frohman. Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0. This record is NOT a proof of global regularity of the 3D Navier-Stokes equations and makes no claim toward the Clay Millennium Problem.
description: DRAFT, NOT PUBLISHED. Lean 4 (v4.30.0-rc1) / Mathlib (v4.30.0-rc1) formalization and manuscript on the Frohmanian tether T(F,G) = -kappa ||omega||^2 int <Pi_u dF, Pi_u dG>, a symmetric quadratic correction to the Arnold Lie-Poisson bracket. Proved: symmetry and negative feedback (C3) unconditionally; canonicity only from diagonal saturation and polarization; and an obstruction to damping: every symmetric kernel satisfying (C2) has B(H,M) = 0 for every functional M. (C1) and (C2) for the tether are not proved. Version 0.1.2 removes hypotheses of earlier versions that were false or vacuous, with Lean refutations where possible: dH/dw = u, transitivity on Casimir levels, the pointwise strain bound |Du(x)| <= C ||omega||_inf, TetherIntegralPreserved, a circular Jacobi lemma, an antisymmetric uniqueness clause (vacuous unless T = 0), and a uniform lower bound on local existence times; it also repairs the definition of a physical solution so that solutions with nonzero initial time derivative qualify. Remaining assumptions are explicit hypotheses: classical results not in Mathlib (Kato local existence, Beale-Kato-Majda continuation, uniqueness, coadjoint motion of Euler), hypotheses as strong as the open problem (the cubic rate and the closing/uniform vorticity bounds), and kernel-class conditions in the canonicity theorems. Build: 2715 jobs; 507 theorem constants (466 stated in the sources, 41 auto-generated) and 750 declarations audited; no sorry, no native_decide, no axiom declarations; only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound (enforced in CI). Not a proof of Navier-Stokes global regularity; no Clay claim.
